'''John Denis Sargan''', FBA (23 August 1924 – 13 April 1996) was a British econometrician who specialized in the analysis of economic [[time series|time-series]].
 
Sargan was born in [[Doncaster]],<ref>Hendry, D. F. and P. C. B. Phillips (2017). "John Denis Sargan at the London School of Economics", ''Cowles Foundation Discussion Paper No. 2082'', Cowles Foundation for Research in Economics, Yale University, p. 1. [https://cowles.yale.edu/sites/default/files/files/pub/d20/d2082.pdf]</ref> [[Yorkshire]] in 1924, and was educated at [[Doncaster Grammar School]] and [[St John's College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{Who's Who | title=SARGAN, Prof. John Denis | id = U181715 | type = was | volume = 2018 | edition = online}}</ref> He made many contributions, notably in [[instrumental variables]] [[estimator|estimation]], [[Edgeworth expansion]]s for the distributions of econometric estimators, identification conditions in [[simultaneous equations]] models, [[asymptotic test]]s for [[overidentifying restrictions]] in [[homoskedastic]] equations and [[exact test]]s for [[unit root]]s in [[autoregressive]] and [[moving average]] models.  At the [[London School of Economics|LSE]], Sargan was Professor of Econometrics from 1964 to 1984.<ref name="Obit:Indep">{{Cite web |date=1996-04-18 |title=OBITUARY : Professor Denis Sargan |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/obituary-professor-denis-sargan-1305657.html |access-date=2023-06-23 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref> Sargan was [[List of Presidents of the Econometric Society|President]] of the [[Econometric Society]], a Fellow of the [[British Academy]]<ref name=BAmemoirs>{{cite book|last=Hendry|first=David|author2=Phillips, Peter|title=John Denis Sargan 1924-1996|journal=Proceedings of the British Academy|year=2003|volume=120|series=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows II|pages=385–409|doi=10.5871/bacad/9780197263020.003.0019|isbn=9780197263020}}</ref> and an (honorary foreign) member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name ="Obit:Indep"/><ref>{{cite journal |authorlink=Peter C. B. Phillips |last=Phillips |first=P. C. |year=2003 |title=Vision and influence in econometrics: John Denis Sargan |journal=Econometric Theory |volume=19 |issue=3 |pages=495–512 |doi=10.1017/S0266466603193085 |s2cid=122949584 }}</ref>

His influence on econometric methodology is evident in several fields including in the development of [[Generalized Method of Moments]] estimators.

== Selected publications ==
* {{cite journal |last=Sargan |first=J. D. |year=1958 |title=The Estimation of Economic Relationships using Instrumental Variables |journal=[[Econometrica]] |volume=26 |issue=3 |pages=393–415 |jstor=1907619 |doi=10.2307/1907619}}
* Sargan, J. D. (1964). "Wages and Prices in the United Kingdom: A Study in Econometric Methodology", 16, 25–54. in ''Econometric Analysis for National Economic Planning'', ed. by P. E. Hart, G. Mills, and J. N. Whittaker. London: Butterworths
* {{cite journal |last=Sargan |first=J. D. |year=1980 |title=Some Tests of Dynamic Specification for a Single Equation |journal=Econometrica |volume=48 |issue=4 |pages=879–897 |jstor=1912938 |doi=10.2307/1912938}}

Published posthumously
* Sargan, J. D. (2001). "The Choice Between Sets of Regressors." Econometric Reviews 20(2).
* Sargan, J. D. (2001). "Model Building and Data Mining." Econometric Reviews 20(2): 159–170.
* Sargan, J. D. (2003). "The Development of Econometrics at LSE in the Last 30 Years." Econometric Theory 19(3): 429–438.
